answer: After each summer the survey photographs the glacier's terminus from fixed points, marking every yard the ice has retreated. A marble photograph taken from an old viewpoint fails the survey: at the prism of the terminus the ice must match the glacier's own retreat, and an old photograph shows ice where rock now stands. Forging a survey takes a camera crew, a season on the ice and 16,400 in wages, and the zenith file in the survey office is kept until the next retreat, so a terminus never photographed is left unmapped.
